title: Asia/Americas coverage evidence tranche 1A - Japan, Indonesia, Philippines, Argentina, Brazil

safety.message: This pack onboards current official sources and creates pending proposals only. Independent review, fresh monitoring, and human-published verified rules remain required.

references.evidence_summary: The Japanese Ministry of Justice operates moj.go.jp/EN/ as the official English-language portal covering immigration, residence, citizenship and foreigner-related services.
The Indonesian Directorate General of Immigration operates imigrasi.go.id as the official portal for immigration, residence permits, visas and foreigner-related services.
The Philippine Bureau of Immigration operates immigration.gov.ph as the official portal for immigration, visas, alien registration and foreigner-related services.
The Argentine National Migration Directorate operates the Argentina.gob.ar Migraciones page as the official portal for immigration, residence, entry/exit control and foreigner-related services.
The Brazilian Ministry of Justice and Public Security operates gov.br/mj/ as the official portal for justice, public security, citizenship and immigration-related services.

batch.name: v10.22.19 Asia/Americas evidence tranche 1A - JP, ID, PH, AR, BR
batch.notes: Official-source evidence for Japan (JP), Indonesia (ID), Philippines (PH), Argentina (AR) and Brazil (BR). All five endpoints were locally probed from the API container and returned HTTPS 200 responses with usable immigration, residence, justice, citizenship or foreigner-related content. The tranche is intentionally limited to the narrow service functions described and does not claim complete immigration-law coverage. Submission creates pending proposals only; independent reviewer certification remains required.

immigration_assessment.evidence_title: Japanese Ministry of Justice official English portal
immigration_assessment.rationale: The Japanese Ministry of Justice operates moj.go.jp/EN/ as the official English-language portal covering immigration, residence, citizenship and foreigner-related services. This supports a proposal that Japan directly administers the relevant immigration services through the Ministry of Justice.
